nodes.label: Unpredictable Symptoms
stories: One day I was completely fine and the next I felt like my body had turned against me. Some weeks it is insomnia and panic attacks, other weeks it is joint pain and exhaustion. I never know what version of myself I am waking up to.
Periods become hellishly and exponentially worse before they stopped. Like 2 days each month couldn't be more than a few steps from the bathroom kind of worse.

I feel like I'm going crazy, I'm 40, got my period 9 days sooner that suppose to, spotting a few days before getting the period and now a week after my period again spotting and my breast are sooo sensitive, like taking my bra off and nipped the nipple and I wanted to cry how painful that was, and not to say I feel bloated and have abdominal.pain as I would get my periods.
For me it was swollen gland under my jaw and neckline that disappeared when my cycle started. Brain fogs where I couldn't remember names. Super insomnia. And scary heart palpitations.

Not sure what is happening to me but I have several symptoms that I've been questioning for a couple years now. 37 here and the list goes: Disrupted sleep, compulsive behavior to check my phone at night. Sugar cravings at night. Occasional night sweats. Either extreme freezing or blazing hot & sweaty. Dry skin. 7-8 day long periods. Digestive issues with crazy bloating. Confusion, especially at work. Urge to use restroom multiple times like I'm prego, also at night. I get migraines so it's hard to tell what is tied to what. Or if it's all just perimenopause. The sensation of bugs crawling on me, also at night. That's a weird one. I just want the madness to stop.

nodes.label: Gaslighting
stories: went to three different doctors over two years. I described migraines, joint pain, brain fog, weight changes, and sudden waves of anxiety. Each symptom was treated separately. I was referred to different specialists, prescribed different medications, and given different explanations.
I had to fight with my doctor and change multiple doctor to get the treatment I wanted.
Doctors kept saying I was too young to be in this phase. The amount of gaslighting and dismissal I have faced is crazy.

After a five-minute appointment, I was told it was probably stress. When I mentioned perimenopause, the doctor said I was too young and suggested I try exercising more. I left feeling embarrassed for bringing it up.

Over the next year, the symptoms got worse. I started forgetting words, waking up drenched in sweat, and avoiding social situations because of my anxiety. It wasn't until I found other women online describing the exact same experiences that I realized I wasn't imagining it. The validation I found from strangers on the internet was something I couldn't get from my healthcare provider.
Looking back, what hurt most was being made to feel unreliable as a narrator of my own body. The symptoms were difficult, but the dismissal made them much harder to carry.
